Components

Modal

A focused overlay that interrupts the workflow to require a response before continuing.

beta
Since 2.1.0 A11y: WCAG 2.2 AA · focus-trap + Escape verified Source: packages/react/src/Modal/Modal.tsx Figma ↗

A Modal is a dialog rendered above the page that traps focus and demands a decision before the user can return to the underlying content. Use it sparingly — it interrupts. For non-blocking messages, prefer a Toast or inline banner.

Beta

Modal is in beta (since 2.1.0). The API is stable, but the dismissOnOverlay default may change to false in 3.0 — set it explicitly.

Live example

The trigger below opens a real modal rendered into a portal. Focus moves to the dialog, Tab is trapped inside it, and Escape closes it.

tsx
import { Modal, Button } from '@halo-ui/react'

function ConfirmDelete() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button tone="danger" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Delete workspace
      </Button>
      <Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
             title="Delete workspace?">
        <p>This permanently removes all 14 projects.</p>
        <Modal.Footer>
          <Button variant="ghost" onClick={close}>Cancel</Button>
          <Button tone="danger" onClick={confirm}>Delete</Button>
        </Modal.Footer>
      </Modal>
    </>
  )
}

Anatomy

A modal has a title (the accessible name), a body, and a footer for actions. The overlay (scrim) dims and blocks the page behind it.

Props

PropTypeDefaultDescription
open*booleanfalseControls visibility. Modal is fully controlled.
onClose*() => void—Called on Escape, overlay click, or close button.
title*string—Accessible name; wired to aria-labelledby.
size'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'fullscreen''md'Max-width of the dialog panel.
dismissOnOverlaybooleantrueWhether clicking the scrim closes the modal.
initialFocusRefObject<HTMLElement>—Element focused when the modal opens.

Behavior

When a modal opens, Halo UI:

  1. Saves the currently focused element to restore later.
  2. Moves focus to initialFocus, or the first focusable child, or the dialog.
  3. Sets aria-hidden="true" and inert on everything outside the dialog.
  4. Traps Tab / Shift+Tab within the dialog.
  5. On close, restores focus to the element from step 1.
tsx
// Focus is restored to the trigger automatically on close.
<Modal open={open} onClose={close} title="Settings" initialFocus={firstFieldRef}>
  …
</Modal>

Guidelines

Do

Use a modal for a single, blocking decision the user must resolve now.

Don't

Stack modals on top of modals — close one before opening the next.

Do

Make the destructive action clearly labeled ("Delete", not "OK").

Don't

Auto-open a modal on page load to show marketing content.

Accessibility

  • Renders role="dialog" with aria-modal="true".
  • title becomes the dialog's aria-labelledby; body text can be referenced via aria-describedby.
  • Escape closes the dialog; focus is trapped while open and restored on close.
  • The scrim has pointer-events enabled so the inert page behind cannot be interacted with — this is what makes it truly modal.

Don't trap users

A modal must always offer a way out — a visible close button, Escape, or a Cancel action. Never remove all three.
